verses.zh: 耶利哥的城门因以色列人就关得严紧，无人出入。
verses.en: Now Jericho[NOTE:1] was shut tightly[NOTE:2] because of the Israelites. No one was allowed to leave or enter.[NOTE:3]
notes: For location see Map5-B2; Map6-E1; Map7-E1; Map8-E3; Map10-A2; Map11-A1.
Heb “was shutting and shut up.” HALOT 743 s.v. I סגר paraphrases, “blocking [any way of access] and blocked [against any who would leave].”
Heb “there was no one going out and there was no one coming in.”
verses.commentary:
6:1-5

6:1-5

6:1-7

6:1-5

6:1-5

6:1 "Jericho was tightly shut because of the sons of Israel" The people had heard
the reports and were fearful (cf. Jos. 2:11; 5:1). Usually at the first sign of danger people from
the surrounding villages rushed into the walled city.

verses.zh: 耶和华晓谕约书亚说：「看哪，我已经把耶利哥和耶利哥的王，并大能的勇士，都交在你手中。
verses.en: The Lord told Joshua, “See, I am about to defeat Jericho for you,[NOTE:1] along with its king and its warriors.
notes: Heb “I have given into your hand Jericho.” The Hebrew verb נָתַתִּי (natatti, “I have given”) is probably best understood as a perfect of certitude, indicating the certainty of the action. The Hebrew pronominal suffix “your” is singular, being addressed to Joshua as the leader and representative of the nation. To convey to the modern reader what is about to happen and who is doing it, the translation “I am about to defeat Jericho for you” has been used.
verses.commentary:
6:2 "The Lord said to Joshua" This is the theophany
angel's message mentioned in Jos. 5:14. This angel, like the one in Exodus 3, speaks for God
(cf. Exod. 3:2,4) and may be a physical manifestation of God (i.e., the Angel of
the Lord).

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE ANGEL OF THE LORD

▣ "See" The VERB (BDB 906, KB 1157, Qal
IMPERATIVE) is characteristic of YHWH's revelations:

- to Moses, Deut. 1:8,21; 2:24; 4:5; 11:26; 30:15; 32:39

- to Joshua, Jos. 6:2; 8:8

It is possibly another way of assuring Joshua that YHWH is with him as He was with Moses.

▣ "I have given Jericho into your hand, with its king and its valiant
warriors" YHWH is asserting the victory ("I have given," BDB 678, KB 733, Qal
PERFECT) even before Jericho falls because He is on their side. However,
there will be a test of obedience as they are commanded in verses 3ff to march around
the city and perform certain acts. The theological emphasis on covenant obedience is
recurrent (cf. Jos. 6:5).

verses.zh: 你们的一切兵丁要围绕这城，一日围绕一次，六日都要这样行。
verses.en: Have all the warriors march around the city one time;[NOTE:1] do this for six days.
notes: Heb “and go around the city, all [you] men of war, encircling the city one time.” The Hebrew verb וְסַבֹּתֶם (vesabbotem, “and go around”) is plural, being addressed to the whole army.

verses.zh: 七个祭司要拿七个羊角走在约柜前。到第七日，你们要绕城七次，祭司也要吹角。
verses.en: Have seven priests carry seven rams’ horns[NOTE:1] in front of the ark. On the seventh day march around the city seven times, while the priests blow the horns.
notes: Heb “rams’ horns, trumpets.”
verses.commentary:
6:4 Notice the repetition of the number "seven" (14 times, see

SPECIAL TOPIC: SYMBOLIC NUMBERS IN SCRIPTURE, #4): seven priests, seven
trumpets, seventh day, and seven times. Seven is the number of perfection or completion
based on Gen. 1:1-2:4. The fall of Jericho is a supernatural act of YHWH, not Israel.

▣ "trumpet of rams' horns" The rabbis stipulate that this must be the
left horn of a male flat-tailed sheep. It was used to remind the synagogue of the lamb that
God used to provide as a substitute for Isaac, Gen. 22:13. It was primarily not a musical
instrument, but a loud blast for religious (cf. Exod. 19:13; Lev. 25:9), and at times,
military purposes.

SPECIAL TOPIC: HORNS USED BY ISRAEL

verses.zh: 他们吹的角声拖长，你们听见角声，众百姓要大声呼喊，城墙就必塌陷，各人都要往前直上。」
verses.en: When you hear the signal from the rams’ horns,[NOTE:1] have the whole army give a loud battle cry.[NOTE:2] Then the city wall will collapse,[NOTE:3] and the warriors should charge straight ahead.”[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “and it will be at the sounding of the horn, the ram’s horn, when you hear the sound of the ram’s horn.” The text of Josh 6:5 seems to be unduly repetitive, so for the sake of English style and readability, it is best to streamline the text here. The reading in the Hebrew looks like a conflation of variant readings, with the second (“when you hear the sound of the ram’s horn”) being an interpolation that assimilates the text to verse 20 (“when the army heard the sound of the horn”). Note that the words “when you hear the sound of the ram’s horn” do not appear in the LXX of verse 5.
Heb “all the people will shout with a loud shout.”
Heb “fall in its place.”
Heb “and the people will go up, each man straight ahead.”
verses.commentary:
6:5 "shout" The term (BDB 929, KB 1206, Hiphil IMPERFECT) is
used to describe a characteristic "war cry" (cf. Jos. 6:10,20; Num. 10:5,9; Jdg. 7:20; 1 Sam. 17:52;
2 Chr. 13:14-15). YHWH used

- the daily marching around the city

- the trumpet sound

- the war cry

- an earthquake

to deliver Jericho into Israel's hands (cf. Jos. 6:2)! Natural things but used with
supernatural intensity, timing, and locality. One good example of a military cry can be seen in
Num. 10:35-36 in connection with the ark.

▣ "the wall of the city will fall down flat" One can almost see the consternation
on the part of the elders when Joshua explained this plan to them, for this was not normal
military procedure! However, it was the word of God and throughout
the Pentateuch we have seen that God has required His people to do that which seems illogical
(cf. Numbers 2) as a test of obedience which shows their faith in His word and promises.

The mechanism for the destruction of the wall was probably an earthquake, but
the timing, intensity, and locality are supernatural (cf., Egyptian plagues and crossing the Jordan).

NASB (UPDATED TEXT): JOSHUA 6:6-11

6So Joshua the son of Nun called the priests and said to them, "Take up the ark of the covenant, and let seven priests carry seven trumpets of rams' horns before the ark of the Lord." 7Then he said to the people, "Go forward, and march around the city, and let the armed men go on before the ark of the Lord." 8And it was so, that when Joshua had spoken to the people, the seven priests carrying the seven trumpets of rams' horns before the Lord went forward and blew the trumpets; and the ark of the covenant of the Lord followed them. 9The armed men went before the priests who blew the trumpets, and the rear guard came after the ark, while they continued to blow the trumpets. 10But Joshua commanded the people, saying, "You shall not shout nor let your voice be heard nor let a word proceed out of your mouth, until the day I tell you, 'Shout!' Then you shall shout!" 11So he had the ark of the Lord taken around the city, circling it once; then they came into the camp and spent the night in the camp.

verses.zh: 嫩的儿子约书亚召了祭司来，吩咐他们说：「你们抬起约柜来，要有七个祭司拿七个羊角走在耶和华的约柜前」；
verses.en: So Joshua son of Nun summoned the priests and instructed them, “Pick up the ark of the covenant, and seven priests must carry seven rams’ horns in front of the ark of the Lord.”
verses.commentary:
6:6-11

6:6-7

6:6-7

6:6-9

6:6-11 This paragraph contains several IMPERATIVES. As YHWH commands
Joshua, he passes them on.

- "take up the ark," Jos. 6:6, BDB 669, KB 724, Qal IMPERATIVE

- "go forward," Jos. 6:7, BDB 716, KB 778, Qal IMPERATIVE

- "march around," Jos. 6:7, BDB 685, KB 738, Qal IMPERATIVE

- "shout," Jos. 6:10, BDB 929, KB 1206, Hiphil IMPERATIVE

6:6 "the ark of the covenant" After the crossing of the Jordan, the Cloud which had
represented YHWH's presence with the people was removed. Now the ark was the visible
symbol of His presence.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE ARK OF THE COVENANT

verses.zh: 又对百姓说：「你们前去绕城，带兵器的要走在耶和华的约柜前。」
verses.en: And he told[NOTE:1] the army,[NOTE:2] “Move ahead[NOTE:3] and march around the city, with armed troops going ahead of the ark of the Lord.”
notes: An alternative reading is “and they said.” In this case the subject is indefinite and the verb should be translated as passive, “[the army] was told.”
Heb “the people.”
Heb “pass by.”
verses.commentary:
6:7 "Then he said to the people" The Masoretic text has "they," which may refer to
the officers mentioned in Jos. 1:10 and 3:2.

verses.zh: 约书亚对百姓说完了话，七个祭司拿七个羊角走在耶和华面前吹角；耶和华的约柜在他们后面跟随。
verses.en: When Joshua gave the army its orders,[NOTE:1] the seven priests carrying the seven rams’ horns before the Lord moved ahead and blew the horns as the ark of the covenant of the Lord followed behind.
notes: Heb “when Joshua spoke to the people.”

verses.zh: 带兵器的走在吹角的祭司前面，后队随着约柜行。祭司一面走一面吹。
verses.en: Armed troops marched ahead of the priests blowing the horns, while the rear guard followed along behind the ark blowing rams’ horns.
verses.commentary:
6:9 "The armed men went before the priests" Two Jewish commentators of the Middle
Ages, Kimchi and Rashi, say that this refers to the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and Manasseh
mentioned in Jos. 4:12-13. This would not have been the normal marching order of the camp.

The term "armed men" (BDB 323, KB 321, Qal PASSIVE PARTICIPLE)
means "fully equipped for battle" (cf. Jos. 6:7,9,13; 4:13; 2 Chr. 20:21; 28:14).

verses.zh: 约书亚吩咐百姓说：「你们不可呼喊，不可出声，连一句话也不可出你们的口，等到我吩咐你们呼喊的日子，那时才可以呼喊。」
verses.en: Now Joshua had instructed the army,[NOTE:1] “Do not give a battle cry[NOTE:2] or raise your voices; say nothing[NOTE:3] until the day I tell you, ‘Give the battle cry.’[NOTE:4] Then give the battle cry!”[NOTE:5]
notes: Heb “the people.”
Or “the shout.”
Heb “do not let a word come out of your mouths.”
Or “the shout.”
Or “the shout.”
verses.commentary:
6:10

6:10 "You shall not shout nor let your voice be heard, nor let a word proceed out of your
mouth, until the day I tell you, 'Shout!'" This same truth must be related to Jos. 6:8,13. Some
people say that this shows that there are two composite accounts, but really what we have are
the priests who could blow the horn every day or at will, and the fighting men who could not
speak until the seventh day!

NASB (UPDATED TEXT): JOSHUA 6:12-14

12Now Joshua rose early in the morning, and the priests took up the ark of the Lord. 13The seven priests carrying the seven trumpets of rams' horns before the ark of the Lord went on continually, and blew the trumpets; and the armed men went before them and the rear guard came after the ark of the Lord, while they continued to blow the trumpets. 14Thus the second day they marched around the city once and returned to the camp; they did so for six days.

verses.zh: 这样，他使耶和华的约柜绕城，把城绕了一次；众人回到营里，就在营里住宿。
verses.en: So Joshua made sure they marched the ark of the Lord around the city one time.[NOTE:1] Then they went back to the camp and spent the night there.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and he made the ark of the Lord go around the city, encircling one time.”
Heb “and they entered the camp and spent the night in the camp.”

verses.zh: 约书亚清早起来，祭司又抬起耶和华的约柜。
verses.en: Bright and early the next morning Joshua had the priests pick up the ark of the Lord.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “Joshua rose early in the morning and the priests picked up the ark of the Lord.”

verses.zh: 七个祭司拿七个羊角在耶和华的约柜前，时常行走吹角；带兵器的在他们前面走，后队随着耶和华的约柜行。祭司一面走一面吹。
verses.en: The seven priests carrying the seven rams’ horns before the ark of the Lord marched along blowing their horns. Armed troops marched ahead of them, while the rear guard followed along behind the ark of the Lord blowing rams’ horns.
verses.commentary:
6:13 "ram's horns" It (BDB 385, see note at Jos. 6:4) was the left horn of a male flat-tailed sheep.

▣ "went" Notice how many times this VERB (BDB 229, KB 246) is
used in this verse—five times. This literary style seems repetitive to moderns.

NASB (UPDATED TEXT): JOSHUA 6:15-21

15Then on the seventh day they rose early at the dawning of the day and marched around the city in the same manner seven times; only on that day they marched around the city seven times. 16At the seventh time, when the priests blew the trumpets, Joshua said to the people, "Shout! For the Lord has given you the city. 17The city shall be under the ban, it and all that is in it belongs to the Lord; only Rahab the harlot and all who are with her in the house shall live, because she hid the messengers whom we sent. 18 But as for you, only keep yourselves from the things under the ban, so that you do not covet them and take some of the things under the ban, and make the camp of Israel accursed and bring trouble on it. 19But all the silver and gold and articles of bronze and iron are holy to the Lord; they shall go into the treasury of the Lord." 20So the people shouted, and priests blew the trumpets; and when the people heard the sound of the trumpet, the people shouted with a great shout and the wall fell down flat, so that the people went up into the city, every man straight ahead, and they took the city. 21They utterly destroyed everything in the city, both man and woman, young and old, and ox and sheep and donkey, with the edge of the sword.

verses.zh: 第二日，众人把城绕了一次，就回营里去。六日都是这样行。
verses.en: They marched around the city one time on the second day, then returned to the camp. They did this six days in all.
verses.commentary:
6:14-16

Jericho Captured and Destroyed

The Fall of Jericho

verses.zh: 第七日清早，黎明的时候，他们起来，照样绕城七次；惟独这日把城绕了七次。
verses.en: On the seventh day they were up at the crack of dawn[NOTE:1] and marched around the city as before—only this time they marched around it seven times.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “On the seventh day they rose early, when the dawn ascended.”
Heb “and they went around the city according to this manner seven times, only on that day they went around the city seven times.”
verses.commentary:
6:15-21

6:15-21

6:15-21

6:15-19
Jericho Placed Under the Curse of Destruction

verses.zh: 到了第七次，祭司吹角的时候，约书亚吩咐百姓说：「呼喊吧，因为耶和华已经把城交给你们了！
verses.en: The seventh time around, the priests blew the rams’ horns, and Joshua told the army,[NOTE:1] “Give the battle cry,[NOTE:2] for the Lord is handing the city over to you![NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “the people.”
Or “the shout.”
Heb “for the Lord has given to you the city.” The verbal form is a perfect, probably indicating certitude here.

verses.zh: 这城和其中所有的都要在耶和华面前毁灭；只有妓女喇合与她家中所有的可以存活，因为她隐藏了我们所打发的使者。
verses.en: The city and all that is in it must be set apart for the Lord;[NOTE:1] only Rahab the prostitute and all who are with her in her house will live, because she hid the spies[NOTE:2] we sent.
notes: Or “dedicated to the Lord.”sn To make the city set apart for the Lord would involve annihilating all the people and animals and placing its riches in the Lord’s treasury (vv. 19, 21, 24).
Heb “messengers.”
verses.commentary:
6:17-19

6:17 "The city shall be under the ban" This is the word herem (BDB 356), which
means "devoted to God for destruction." It is the concept of holy war where everything in the city
that breathed must die because it is given to God and, therefore, it becomes too holy for human
use. The one exception is Rahab, the harlot, and her family, because of the help she gave to the
spies and their oath in YHWH's name to protect her.

SPECIAL TOPIC: CURSE (OT)

verses.zh: 至于你们，务要谨慎，不可取那当灭的物，恐怕你们取了那当灭的物就连累以色列的全营，使全营受咒诅。
verses.en: But be careful when you are setting apart the riches for God. If you take any of it, then you will make the Israelite camp subject to annihilation and cause a disaster.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “Only you keep [away] from what is set apart [to God] so that you might not, as you are setting [it] apart, take some of what is set apart [to God] and turn the camp of Israel into what is set apart [to destruction by God] and bring trouble on it.”
verses.commentary:
6:18 "keep yourselves from the things under the ban" YHWH's people must
restrain (BDB 1036, KB 1581, Qal IMPERATIVE) themselves.
Joshua 7 will describe the consequences of disobedience!

verses.zh: 惟有金子、银子，和铜铁的器皿都要归耶和华为圣，必入耶和华的库中。」
verses.en: All the silver and gold, as well as bronze and iron items, belong to the Lord.[NOTE:1] They must go into the Lord’s treasury.”
notes: Heb “it is holy to the Lord.”

verses.zh: 于是百姓呼喊，祭司也吹角。百姓听见角声，便大声呼喊，城墙就塌陷，百姓便上去进城，各人往前直上，将城夺取；
verses.en: The rams’ horns sounded,[NOTE:1] and when the army[NOTE:2] heard the signal,[NOTE:3] they gave a loud battle cry.[NOTE:4] The wall collapsed,[NOTE:5] and the warriors charged straight ahead into the city and captured it.[NOTE:6]
notes: Heb “and the people shouted and they blew the rams’ horns.” The initial statement (“and the people shouted”) seems premature, since the verse goes on to explain that the battle cry followed the blowing of the horns. The statement has probably been accidentally duplicated from what follows. It is omitted in the LXX.
Heb “the people.”
Heb “the sound of the horn.”
Heb “they shouted with a loud shout.”
Heb “fell in its place.”
Heb “and the people went up into the city, each one straight ahead, and they captured the city.”
verses.commentary:
6:20-21

6:20-21

Rahab Spared

Rahab's House Preserved

verses.zh: 又将城中所有的，不拘男女老少，牛羊和驴，都用刀杀尽。
verses.en: They annihilated with the sword everything that breathed in the city,[NOTE:1] including men and women, young and old, as well as cattle, sheep, and donkeys.
notes: Heb “all which was in the city.”
verses.commentary:
6:21 This is a description of holy war. It seems very cruel to us in our day, but
one must remember that it was a common military practice in the day in which it was
done (e.g., Moabite inscription from Mesha, KAI 181:17). It was also an act of divine
judgment based on Gen. 15:16. That which was given to YHWH became holy and could
not be used by humans (cf. Lev. 27:28-29).

NASB (UPDATED TEXT): JOSHUA 6:22-25

22 Joshua said to the two men who had spied out the land, "Go into the harlot's house and bring the woman and all she has out of there, as you have sworn to her." 23So the young men who were spies went in and brought out Rahab and her father and her mother and her brothers and all she had; they also brought out all her relatives and placed them outside the camp of Israel. 24They burned the city with fire, and all that was in it. Only the silver and gold, and articles of bronze and iron, they put into the treasury of the house of the Lord. 25However, Rahab the harlot and her father's household and all she had, Joshua spared; and she has lived in the midst of Israel to this day, for she hid the messengers whom Joshua sent to spy out Jericho.

verses.zh: 约书亚吩咐窥探地的两个人说：「你们进那妓女的家，照着你们向她所起的誓，将那女人和她所有的都从那里带出来。」
verses.en: Joshua told the two men who had spied on the land, “Enter the prostitute’s house[NOTE:1] and bring out the woman and all who belong to her as you promised her.”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “the house of the woman, the prostitute.”
Heb “and bring out from there the woman and all who belong to her as you swore on oath to her.”
verses.commentary:
6:22-25

6:22-25

6:22-25

6:22-25

6:22-23

6:22 "Go. . .bring" These are two more IMPERATIVES. Joshua is
present and directing the course of events.

- "go into," BDB 97, KB 112, Qal IMPERATIVE

- "bring out," BDB 422, KB 425, Qal IMPERATIVE

verses.zh: 当探子的两个少年人就进去，将喇合与她的父母、弟兄，和她所有的，并她一切的亲眷，都带出来，安置在以色列的营外。
verses.en: So the young spies went and brought out Rahab, her father, mother, brothers, and all who belonged to her. They brought out her whole family and took them to a place outside[NOTE:1] the Israelite camp.
notes: Or “placed them outside.”
verses.commentary:
6:23 "the young men" This term (BDB 654) denotes a young person under the
supervision of another. However, in Jos. 2:1,3; 6:22, they are called "men" (BDB 35). It is
possible that the term does not refer to age in this context, but to these spies who must
report back to Joshua.

▣ "and placed them outside the camp of Israel" Because Rahab, at this point,
was still a Canaanite, and, therefore, ceremonially unclean, she was removed from the holy
people for a time (cf. Deut. 23:14). However, Jos. 6:25 shows that she was later fully included
in the covenant community (people can change/be changed!).

verses.zh: 众人就用火将城和其中所有的焚烧了；惟有金子、银子，和铜铁的器皿都放在耶和华殿的库中。
verses.en: But they burned[NOTE:1] the city and all that was in it, except for the silver, gold, and bronze and iron items they put in the treasury of the Lord’s house.[NOTE:2]
notes: The Hebrew text adds “with fire.”
Heb “the treasury of the house of the Lord.” Technically the Lord did not have a “house” yet, so perhaps this refers to the tabernacle using later terminology.
verses.commentary:
6:24-25

A Curse on Anyone Who Rebuilds Jericho

6:24 Burning was a sign of the herem (ban, cf. Deut. 13:16). That which was
physical was turned into the invisible and rose up in smoke to God. Several cities were
burned by Joshua (Jericho, Ai, 8:28; Hazor, 11:6,9,11,13). However, not all cities were dedicated
to YHWH. Israel inhabited many Canaanite cities.

SPECIAL TOPIC: FIRE

▣ "the house of the Lord" This obviously refers
to the tabernacle here (cf. Exod. 25-27), but in the OT it usually refers to the temple in Jerusalem.

NASB (UPDATED TEXT): JOSHUA 6:26-27

26Then Joshua made them take an oath at that time, saying, "Cursed before the Lord is the man who rises up and builds this city Jericho; with the loss of his firstborn he shall lay its foundation, and with the loss of his youngest son he shall set up its gates." 27So the Lord was with Joshua, and his fame was in all the land.

verses.zh: 约书亚却把妓女喇合与她父家，并她所有的，都救活了；因为她隐藏了约书亚所打发窥探耶利哥的使者，她就住在以色列中，直到今日。
verses.en: Yet Joshua spared[NOTE:1] Rahab the prostitute, her father’s family,[NOTE:2] and all who belonged to her. She lives in Israel[NOTE:3] to this very day because she hid the messengers Joshua sent to spy on Jericho.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “kept alive.”
Heb the house of her father.”
Or “among the Israelites”; Heb “in the midst of Israel.”
For location see Map5-B2; Map6-E1; Map7-E1; Map8-E3; Map10-A2; Map11-A1.

verses.zh: 当时，约书亚叫众人起誓说：「有兴起重修这耶利哥城的人，当在耶和华面前受咒诅。他立根基的时候，必丧长子，安门的时候，必丧幼子。」
verses.en: At that time Joshua made this solemn declaration:[NOTE:1] “The man who attempts to rebuild[NOTE:2] this city of Jericho[NOTE:3] will stand condemned before the Lord.[NOTE:4] He will lose his firstborn son when he lays its foundations and his youngest son when he erects its gates!”[NOTE:5]
notes: Normally the Hiphil of שָׁבַע (shavaʿ) has a causative sense (“make [someone] take an oath”; see Josh 2:17, 20), but here (see also Josh 23:7) no object is stated or implied. If Joshua is calling divine judgment down upon the one who attempts to rebuild Jericho, then “make a solemn appeal [to God as judge]” or “pronounce a curse” would be an appropriate translation. However, the tone seems stronger. Joshua appears to be announcing the certain punishment of the violator. 1 Kgs 16:34, which records the fulfillment of Joshua’s prediction, supports this. Casting Joshua in a prophetic role, it refers to Joshua’s statement as the “word of the Lord” spoken through Joshua.
Heb “rises up and builds.”
The LXX omits “Jericho.” It is probably a scribal addition.
The Hebrew phrase אָרוּר לִפְנֵי יְהוָה (ʾarur lifne yehvah, “cursed [i.e., condemned] before the Lord”) also occurs in 1 Sam 26:19.

Heb “With his firstborn he will lay its foundations and with his youngest he will erect its gates.” The Hebrew verb יַצִּיב (yatsiv, “he will erect”) is imperfect, not jussive, suggesting Joshua’s statement is a prediction, not an imprecation.

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which
means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the
light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not
relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare
your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is
the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every
paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- Joshua 6-12 describe the major military campaigns of Joshua.

- The first half of the book of Joshua, Joshua 1-12, describes the entering into
(Joshua 1-5) and conquest (Joshua 6-12) of the Promised Land. There are three
distinct geographical movements of Joshua's army.

- the central campaign, Joshua 6-8

- Jericho

- Ai

- covenant ceremony at Shechem

- the southern campaign, Joshua 9-10

- Gibeon ruse

- the five kings

- the northern campaign, chapters Jos. 11:1-15

- Hazor

- summary, Jos. 11:16-23; 12:1-24

- Notice the number of double VERBALS of the same root in this
chapter. This is a characteristic of Joshua.

- "tightly shut," Jos. 6:1, BDB 688, KB 742, Qal PERFECT and
Pual PARTICIPLE

- "take up," Jos. 6:6, BDB 669, KB 724, Qal IMPERATIVE and
Qal IMPERFECT

- "blew," Jos. 6:9, BDB 1075, KB 1785, Qal PERFECT and
Qal PARTICIPLE

- "walk," Jos. 6:9, BDB 229, KB 246, Qal PARTICIPLE and
Qal INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE

- "shout," Jos. 6:10, BDB 929, KB 1206, Hiphil IMPERATIVE and
Hiphil PERFECT

- "took up," Jos. 6:12-13, BDB 669, KB 724, Qal IMPERFECT and
Qal PARTICIPLE

- "went," Jos. 6:13, BDB 229, KB 246, Qal PARTICIPLE and
Qal INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE (twice)

- "brought out," Jos. 6:23, BDB 422, KB 425, Hiphil IMPERFECT
and Hiphil PERFECT

- "was," Jos. 6:27, BDB 224, KB 242, Qal IMPERFECT and
Qal IMPERFECT

This kind of repetition is common throughout the book. See note at Jos. 3:15.

6:27 This refers to the fear of the Canaanite population ("their hearts melted").

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible
for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy
Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this
section of the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- What is significant about the unusual military procedure used to capture Jericho?

- Why is Rahab such a wonderful example of God's grace?

- Describe the procedure and reason for "holy war."
